correctness.rationale: Exact integral calculations B²=5(B+I), detB=-5, C1=[[836,1353],[1353,2189]], det C1=-605 establish the base. Binomial lifting and Cj²≡0 mod5 show Cj≡C1 mod25 for j≥1, giving Smith valuations (j,j+1). Their fixed-point kernels and the mod-five eigenvalue order-four obstruction partition every period and account for all 5^(2k) states. The extracted finite verifier checks 406900 states and 14 fixed-point calculations; finite checks are supporting evidence only.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general class equation constrains the weighted sum of cycle multiplicities but does not imply the individual five-adic fixed-point counts and thus cannot by itself force the proposed census. The 2-adic composite-modulus result is not a stronger specialization for 5^k. A broader uninspected theorem on Smith forms could nevertheless imply the formula.

originality.rationale: OEIS A015134 explicitly labels the identical total-cycle formula as a conjecture. Coleman et al. 2006 supply the generic orbit class equation and a four-cycle but do not yield all local fixed-point valuations; the accessible similar 3·2^k finding has a different p-adic domain. Targeted published-finding corpus searches did not reveal an equivalent/higher theorem, without implying exhaustive uniqueness.
residual_risks: A published general theorem on Smith valuations for repeated-root Lucas companion matrices could imply the five-adic census without mentioning this OEIS sequence.
Source comparisons and semantic searches do not certify exhaustive priority; a separate independent audit is not performed.

value.rationale: The result settles a documented infinite-family conjecture for a natural number-theoretic recurrence and gives every period and multiplicity, substantially sharper than the total or finite OEIS tables. The proof isolates the ramified characteristic-five Smith invariants and supplies a reusable local dynamic method; not a routine parameter substitution.
